pageTitle: Determine the Area of Parallelograms and Rhombuses
covers: how to find the area of a parallelogram or rhombus using base times perpendicular height, not the slanted side

intro.caption: Lesson 5-1 — area of parallelograms and rhombuses. The build-off roof leans at an angle, Gel already ate half the blueprint, and Dree wants to order blocks by the slanted edge. Three gates and a supply-counter boss stand between the crew and a dry roof.

balloons.t: Our roof is a parallelogram. We need the exact area before we order roof blocks.
Blurb! Blueprint tastes like graph paper and pine.
Easy! Base is 12, slanted side is 7. Twelve times seven is 84!
Hold on! Watch what happens when I slide this triangle to the other side.

pages.caption: Dree multiplied by the slanted side. Sliding one triangle to the other end turns a parallelogram into a rectangle.

balloons.t: Same area, new shape! The rectangle uses the straight-up height, not the slant.
A rhombus is a parallelogram too. My square finds the perpendicular height at 90 degrees.
So even when all four sides are 9, we only multiply base by straight-up height!
Okay, no slants! What if we already know the area and need the height?
Then divide area by base. Base times height works both ways!
We ordered 150 square blocks for a 15-by-10 roof. Beat that, rookies!
Blurb! That 10 is the slanted side. Height is 7!
Every block fits, zero extras left over, and Gel only ate two blueprints.

win.caption: A parallelogram (including a rhombus) rearranges into a rectangle with the same base and perpendicular height, so Area = base × height.

gates.title: Gate 1 · Shear to a Rectangle
gates.prompt: Use Ana's rectangle trick to find the area of the roof panel (base 12, perpendicular height 5, slanted side 7).
hints: Conceptual: cutting a right triangle off one end of a parallelogram and sliding it to the other end makes a rectangle with the same area.
Procedural: multiply the base by the straight-up perpendicular height (A = b × h). Ignore the slanted side.

steps: Practice panel: base = 7 blocks, perpendicular height = 4 blocks, slanted side = 6 blocks.
Slide the end triangle to make a 7 by 4 rectangle.
worked.q: A parallelogram has base 9 and perpendicular height 3. What is its area?

items.q: When you cut a triangle off one side of a parallelogram and slide it to the other side, what shape do you make?

options.t: A trapezoid with a bigger area
options.fb: Sliding a piece keeps the exact same area, and opposite sides stay parallel.

options.t: A rectangle with the same base and height
A triangle with half the area
options.fb: You moved the piece, not removed it. The total area stays the same.

options.t: A square using the slanted side
options.fb: The straight cut forms 90-degree corners with the base and perpendicular height, not the slant.

items.label: Roof panel area (b = 12, h = 5, slant = 7):
items.aria: area of parallelogram roof panel in square blocks

fb.msg: 84 is 12 × 7, using the slanted side. Use the perpendicular height (5) instead.
17 is 12 + 5. Area multiplies base and height rather than adding them.
38 is the perimeter 2 × (12 + 7). Area measures the inside space, not the border.

items.fbDefault: Multiply the base (12) by the perpendicular height (5).

gates.pass: Sixty square blocks! Dree quietly puts the extra 24 blocks back on the cart.

gates.title: Gate 2 · Find the Height
gates.prompt: Kai's carpenter square always checks for a 90° angle. Find the area of Moss's rhombus wall tile.
hints: Conceptual: a rhombus is a parallelogram with four equal sides, so its area formula is still base × perpendicular height.
Procedural: pick the height that meets the base at a 90° right angle, then multiply b × h.

steps: Practice tile: base = 6, slanted side = 8, perpendicular height = 5.
Skip the slanted 8 because it does not meet the base at 90°.
worked.q: A parallelogram has base 8, slanted side 10, and height 6. Find its area.

items.q: Which measurement is the height of a parallelogram?

options.t: The longest side of the shape
options.fb: The longest side might be the base or the slanted edge, not the height.

options.t: The slanted edge leaning from bottom to top
options.fb: A slanted edge is longer than the straight-up distance and is never the height.

options.t: The perpendicular (90°) distance from the base to the opposite side

items.label: Rhombus tile area (base = 9, slant = 9, height = 4):
items.aria: area of rhombus wall tile in square blocks

fb.msg: 81 is 9 × 9, using the slanted side. Only a square with 90° corners has area side × side.
13 is 9 + 4. Multiply base by height to find area.

items.fbDefault: Multiply the base (9) by the perpendicular height (4).

gates.pass: Thirty-six square blocks for the rhombus tile. Kai snaps his square shut.

gates.title: Gate 3 · Compute & Reverse
gates.prompt: Compute the main roof section and find the missing height for the side awning.
hints: Conceptual: A = b × h links three numbers. If you know Area and base, dividing Area ÷ base gives the height.
Procedural: multiply base × perpendicular height for the main roof, and divide 54 ÷ 9 for the awning.

steps: Practice awning: area = 40 square blocks, base = 8 blocks.
worked.q: A parallelogram has area 45 and base 9. What is its height?

items.label: Main roof (base = 14, slant = 11, height = 8). Area =
items.aria: area of main roof in square blocks

fb.msg: 154 is 14 × 11, using the slanted side. Use the perpendicular height (8).
22 is 14 + 8. Multiply base by height instead of adding.

items.label: Side awning (area = 54, base = 9). Height =

fb.msg: 486 is 54 × 9. When area is already given, divide by the base to find height.
45 is 54 − 9. Undo multiplication by dividing, not subtracting.

items.fbDefault: Divide the area (54) by the base (9).

gates.pass: 112 square blocks on top and a 6-block height on the awning. Ready for the supply counter!

gates.title: Boss Gate · Order the Blocks
gates.prompt: The Champs ordered 150 square blocks for a roof with base 15, slanted side 10, and perpendicular height 7. Fix their order and buy the right bundles.
hints: Conceptual: always check which measurement is at 90° to the base before multiplying, then divide total area by bundle size.
Procedural: first find Area = 15 × 7. Then divide that area by 5 square blocks per bundle.

steps: Practice roof: area = 36 square blocks. Each bundle covers 3 square blocks.
worked.q: A 42-square-block roof uses 6-square-block bundles. How many bundles?

items.label: Lock 1 · True area (b = 15, slant = 10, h = 7):
items.aria: true area of the Champs roof in square blocks

fb.msg: 150 is 15 × 10, The Champs' mistake! 10 is the slanted side, not the perpendicular height.
50 is the perimeter 2 × (15 + 10). Area is base × perpendicular height.

items.label: Lock 2 · Bundles needed (5 sq blocks each):

fb.msg: 30 bundles would cover 150 square blocks — that's The Champs' wrong order.
525 is 105 × 5. Divide the total area by 5 to count bundles.

items.fbDefault: Divide 105 square blocks by 5 square blocks per bundle.

items.q: Lock 3 · Why did The Champs waste 45 square blocks of roofing?

options.fb: Parallelograms do not divide by 2 — that's for triangles.

options.t: They multiplied by the slanted side instead of the perpendicular height
They added the base and the height
options.fb: Adding 15 + 7 would be 22, which is way too small, not 150.

gates.pass: 105 square blocks, 21 bundles, zero waste. The Champs stare at their giant stack of extra blocks.

journal.heading: Lesson 5-1 — what the slanted roof taught us
rows: Area of a parallelogram = base × height (A = b × h), including rhombuses.
Cutting a triangle off one end and sliding it to the other makes a rectangle with the same base and height.
The height must meet the base at a 90° right angle — straight up, never leaning.
Never use the slanted side as the height. The slanted edge is longer and makes the area too big.
journal.quote: "The blueprint was delicious, but 90 degrees is the real secret." — Gel

teacher.suggested: Use during or after lesson 5-1 (Determine the Area of Parallelograms and Rhombuses). Whole-class on a projector, pairs on devices, or independent practice. Covers parallelogram and rhombus area via shearing to a rectangle, distinguishing perpendicular height from slanted sides, and finding a missing height.
standards: Derive a formula for the area of a right triangle using a rectangle; find the area of triangles and special quadrilaterals by decomposing or composing
